gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: Gross profit increased $7.2 million or 2.6% in the second quarter and increased $67.4 million or 12.7% in the six months of fiscal 2027 compared to the comparable periods of fiscal 2026. Gross profit, as a percentage of net sales, increased 80 basis points in the second quarter and increased 290 basis points in six months of fiscal 2027, compared to the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2026. The increase to the gross profit margin for the quarter and six months is primarily related to greater impact of IRC 45X benefits, and IEEPA tariff refunds compared to the prior periods.

opex.text: Operating expenses, as a percentage of sales, decreased 160 basis points in the second quarter and decreased 180 basis points in six months of fiscal 2027, compared to the comparable periods of fiscal 2026. Our operating expenses for the second quarter and six months decreased as a percentage of sales due to our cost saving and restructuring initiatives.

costs.text: Operating expenses, as a percentage of sales, decreased 160 basis points in the second quarter and decreased 180 basis points in six months of fiscal 2027, compared to the comparable periods of fiscal 2026. Our operating expenses for the second quarter and six months decreased as a percentage of sales due to our cost saving and restructuring initiatives.

nonint.text: Operating expenses, as a percentage of sales, decreased 160 basis points in the second quarter and decreased 180 basis points in six months of fiscal 2027, compared to the comparable periods of fiscal 2026. Our operating expenses for the second quarter and six months decreased as a percentage of sales due to our cost saving and restructuring initiatives.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense of $10.1 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (net of interest income of $2.8 million) was $(2.1) million lower than the interest expense of 12.2 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 (net of interest income of $3.3 million).

Interest expense of $20.7 million in the six months of fiscal 2027 (net of interest income of $7.0 million) was $(2.8) million lower than the interest expense of $23.5 million in the six months of fiscal 2026 (net of interest income of $6.4 million).

The decrease in interest expense in the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2027 is primarily due to lower borrowing levels in the quarter and higher interest income in the year. Our average debt outstanding was $1,019.0 million and $1,078 in the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2027, compared to $1,314.0 million and $1,234.7 million in the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2026.

Included in interest expense are non-cash charges for deferred financing fees of $0.6 million and $1.1 for the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2027 and $0.5 million and $1.0 million in the second quarter and six months of fiscal 2026.

tax.heading: Earnings Before Income Taxes
tax.text: As a result of the above, earnings before income taxes in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 increased $26.2 million, or 34.1%, compared to the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and increased $95.5 million, or 67.1% in the six months of fiscal 2027 compared to the six months of fiscal 2026.

ocf.text: A substantial majority of the Company’s cash and investments are held by foreign subsidiaries and are considered to be indefinitely reinvested and expected to be utilized to fund local operating activities, capital expenditure requirements and acquisitions. The Company believes that it has sufficient sources of domestic and foreign liquidity.

da.text: During fiscal 2027, the Company recorded $0.5 million primarily relating to retention costs and $6.9 million in accelerated depreciation of fixed assets.

wc.text: In the first six months of fiscal 2026, operating activities provided cash of $219.0 million with the decrease in operating cash resulting mainly due to activity in accounts receivable, inventory, prepaid and other current assets, accrued expenses and accounts payable. Inventory increased or used cash of $48.7 million, and accounts receivable decreased or provided cash of $43.7 million. Additionally, accounts payable decreased or used cash of $34.7 million. In the six months of fiscal 2026, net earnings were $125.9 million, depreciation and amortization $54.9 million, stock-based compensation $22.0 million, and $2.1 million in cash proceeds from derivatives not designated in hedging relationships. Prepaid and other current assets provided funds of $69.5 million, primarily from a decrease of $81.4 million in prepaid taxes included $137.0 million payment from the IRS relating to prior year tax return refund, and $16.4 million in contract assets, partially offset by a decrease of $3.1 million in other prepaid expenses and $3.0 million in non trade receivables. Accrued expenses were a use of funds of $21.4 million primarily from a decrease in tax accruals of $34.7 million and sales related accruals of $5.3 million, partially offset by increases of $12.6 million to restructuring accruals, $5.6 million to miscellaneous other accruals, and $3.9 million in freight.

capex.text: Investing activities used cash of $24.6 million in the six months of fiscal 2027, which primarily consisted of capital expenditures of $24.8 million relating to plant improvements.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Net sales decreased $1.4 million or 0.1% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 as compared to the second quarter of fiscal 2026. This decrease was the result of a decrease from foreign currency translation.

Net sales increased $41.2 million or 2.2% in the six months of fiscal 2027 as compared to the six months of fiscal 2026. This increase was due to a 1% increase in pricing, and a 1% increase in organic volume.

intro.text: EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs with batteries, chargers and other power equipment. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter. For more information, visit www.enersys.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our customer base is highly diverse, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of our revenues.
Approximately 40% of net sales were generated outside of the United States in fiscal 2026.
Our ability to maintain and improve our operating margins depends on our ability to control and reduce our costs in addition to our ability to maintain business relationships with customers.

We depend on third parties, including suppliers, distributors, lead toll operators, freight forwarders, insurance brokers, commodity brokers, major financial institutions and other third party service providers, for key aspects of our business, including the provision of derivative contracts to manage risks of commodity cost volatility, foreign currency exposures and interest rate volatility.

Our plan to grow the volume and profitability of our energy storage products depends on significant lithium-ion battery cell production, including by our partner Verkor SAS at a proposed gigafactory in South Carolina.

We rely on a combination of copyright, trademark, patent and trade secret laws, non-disclosure agreements and other confidentiality procedures and contractual provisions to establish, protect and maintain our proprietary intellectual property and technology and other confidential information.
The success of our business depends upon the quality of our products and our relationships with customers.
We rely upon a combination of trademark, licensing and contractual covenants to establish and protect the brand names of our products.

We rely on our production facilities, as well as third-party suppliers and manufacturers, in the United States, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, the People’s Republic of China (“PRC”), the United Kingdom and other countries that were significantly impacted by COVID-19.

Sales of our motive power products, for example, depend significantly on demand for new electric industrial forklift trucks, which in turn depends on end-user demand for additional motive capacity in their distribution and manufacturing facilities.

Our ability to continue our ongoing business operations and fund future growth depends on our ability to maintain adequate credit facilities and to comply with the financial and other covenants in such credit facilities or to secure alternative sources of financing.

In addition, our ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance our debt obligations depends on our financial condition and operating performance, which is subject to prevailing economic and competitive conditions and to financial, business, legislative, regulatory and other factors, some of which are beyond our control.
Our ability to successfully penetrate new geographic markets may depend on new countries adopting, to the extent such incentives are not currently in place and maintaining such incentives.
We depend on our senior management team and other key employees, and significant attrition within our management team or unsuccessful succession planning could adversely affect our business.

However, the payment and amount of future dividends remain within the discretion of the Board and will depend upon the Company's future earnings, financial condition, capital requirements, restrictions under existing or future credit facilities or debt and other factors.
We estimate that a 10% increase in our cost of lead would have increased our cost of goods sold by approximately $65 million for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.
